name: Bark (Suno)
description: Generative TTS that can produce highly expressive speech, music, and sound effects. Very creative but slower.

name: Canary 1B v2
description: NVIDIA multilingual ASR + speech translation in a single model. 25 European languages, bidirectional EN↔XX translation. Tops Open ASR Leaderboard multilingual category. Word-level timestamps, punctuation & capitalization.

name: Chatterbox TTS
description: Open-source SOTA voice cloning from Resemble AI. Outperforms ElevenLabs on naturalness benchmarks. Supports emotion exaggeration control and ultra-stable generation.

name: ChatTTS
description: Conversational TTS optimized for dialogue with natural turn-taking and emotion. Great for chatbots.

name: Cohere Transcribe 03-2026
description: Open-weights Conformer ASR model (speech-to-text), not a TTS model. Converts speech audio into transcribed text with multilingual support.
context: Input: audio waveform -> log-Mel spectrogram; 2B params

name: Coqui TTS (XTTS v2)
description: The most popular open TTS with incredible voice cloning from just 6 seconds of audio. Discontinued but widely used.

name: CosyVoice 2
description: Industrial-grade multilingual TTS with streaming, voice cloning and emotion control. Exceptional Chinese + English quality. Used in production at Alibaba scale.

name: Dia
description: 1.6B dialogue TTS — generates realistic two-speaker conversations from a single transcript. Supports non-verbal cues like [laughs], [coughs], [sighs] natively.

name: Edge TTS
description: Python interface to Microsoft Edge's online TTS. Not fully local but works offline with cached voices.

name: EmotiVoice
description: Multi-voice TTS with granular emotion control. Choose from 2000+ built-in voices and specify emotions like happy, sad, angry, or surprised per sentence.

name: eSpeak NG
description: Compact, fast rule-based TTS. Not neural but extremely lightweight and supports 100+ languages.

name: F5-TTS
description: Flow-matching based TTS with SOTA quality and extremely fast inference. Simple and efficient architecture.

name: F5-TTS v1.1
description: Iterative upgrade over the original F5-TTS. Faster convergence via improved flow-matching schedule, better Chinese prosody, cross-lingual cloning. Now with streaming inference and improved CFM sampler.

name: Fish Speech
description: Fast, high-quality TTS with voice cloning and multilingual support. Optimized for real-time applications.

name: GPT-SoVITS
description: Zero-shot voice cloning TTS combining GPT and SoVITS. Clone any voice from 5 seconds of audio. Extremely popular in the open-source community with 40K+ GitHub stars.

name: Granite Speech 4.1 2B
description: Compact Apache 2.0 speech-language model for multilingual ASR and bidirectional speech translation. Adds punctuation, truecasing, keyword biasing and Japanese ASR improvements.
context: 2B speech-language model for ASR, AST, punctuation, truecasing and keyword-biased recognition

name: Higgs Audio v2
description: SOTA expressive TTS built on an LLM-audio backbone. Generates natural multi-speaker dialogue, spontaneous laughter, whispers and even background music. Beats ElevenLabs on MOS naturalness in several languages.
context: LLM backbone with audio tokenizer, 3B params

name: IndexTTS 2
description: Bilibili's viral open TTS — exceptional zero-shot cloning and emotion transfer. Separately controls voice timbre and emotional style from two different reference clips. Top quality on Chinese + English.

name: IndicTTS
description: Multi-Indian language TTS supporting Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Marathi and more. High quality for Indian languages often underserved by other models. Built at IIT Madras.

name: Kitten TTS
description: Tiny open-source TTS built for edge devices. Three variants: 80M, 40M, and 14M params — the smallest fits in under 25 MB. Highly expressive despite its size. Runs entirely on CPU, no GPU required. Perfect for embedded systems, mobile, and offline apps.

name: Kokoro TTS
description: Ultra-lightweight yet stunning quality. 82M params only — runs on CPU in real-time. Best quality-to-size ratio of any TTS model.

name: Kyutai STT 2.6B
description: Production-grade streaming ASR from Kyutai (makers of Moshi). Delay-streaming transformer with 500ms latency, word-level timestamps, speaker diarization. Top of Open ASR Leaderboard for real-time French + English.

name: LLaSA 3B
description: LLaMA-based TTS with pure next-token speech generation — no separate decoder. Scales with compute: the 3B variant matches specialised TTS SOTA on zero-shot cloning. Trained on 250K hours of Chinese + English speech.

name: MARS5
description: AR-diffusion hybrid TTS with near-human quality. Ultra-fast zero-shot voice cloning from a few seconds of audio. Unique hybrid architecture combining autoregressive and diffusion.

name: MaskGCT
description: Fully non-autoregressive TTS — no text-phone alignment needed. Achieves human parity on naturalness and similarity metrics. Incredibly fast inference.

name: MeloTTS
description: High-quality multilingual TTS with extremely natural voice cloning. Best for Chinese and English with fast inference.

name: MetaVoice-1B
description: 1B parameter TTS with zero-shot voice cloning. Large model for high-quality synthesis.

name: MisoTTS
description: 8B English-first emotive conversational TTS model designed for natural dialogue, voice continuation from prompt audio and private local speech experiments. Excellent quality signal, but heavier than small TTS models and best on CUDA GPUs or larger Apple Silicon setups.
voices: Emotive English dialogue + prompt audio continuation
context: 8B text-to-dialogue RVQ Transformer, Mimi audio tokenizer, 2048 max sequence length

name: MMS (Meta)
description: Massively Multilingual Speech by Meta. Supports 1100+ languages, the most comprehensive language coverage available.

name: Moshi
description: Full-duplex spoken dialogue model — listens and speaks simultaneously with ~160 ms latency. Not just a TTS but a real-time conversational speech model. Runs on a single L4 GPU or Mac M3 Pro.

name: MOSS-TTS-Nano
description: Tiny 0.1B multilingual speech generation model for CPU-friendly real-time TTS. Supports voice cloning, streaming, ONNX CPU inference and MLX Audio on Apple Silicon.
context: 0.1B params, 20 languages, ONNX CPU version runs smoothly on MacBook Air M4

name: NeuTTS Air
description: First super-realistic TTS LLM that runs in real-time on CPU. 748M params, LLaMA 3.2 backbone + NeuCodec audio tokenizer. GGUF-native — perfect for on-device agents and offline apps. Instant 3s voice cloning.

name: OCTAVE 2
description: Second-gen emotion-aware speech-language model. Generates voice, style and personality from a text description alone — no reference audio required. Rich control over arousal, valence and speaking style. Research-first release.
context: Describe a speaker in natural language

name: OpenVoice V2
description: Cross-lingual voice cloning — clone a voice in one language and speak any other. Granular style control (emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses). Very fast inference, GPU-optional.

name: Orpheus TTS
description: LLM-based TTS with human-level naturalness. Supports rich emotion tags (laugh, sigh, hesitation). Built on Llama 3 architecture for unprecedented expressiveness.

name: OuteTTS
description: Pure language model approach to TTS — no separate audio encoder. Runs via llama.cpp for fully local GGUF inference. Excellent for CPU-only setups.

name: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2
description: NVIDIA's SOTA lightweight ASR — 0.6B params, #1 on Open ASR Leaderboard for English. TDT (Token-and-Duration Transducer) decoding makes it 50× faster than Whisper Large v3 on GPU. Real-time streaming with word-level timestamps.

name: Parler TTS
description: High-quality controllable TTS trained on 10k+ hours of audiobooks. Natural prosody and speaker control via prompts.

name: Piper
description: Fast, local neural TTS optimized for Raspberry Pi and edge devices. Lightweight with good quality for embedded systems.

name: Qwen3-ASR
description: Open-source ASR family with 0.6B and 1.7B models. Supports language identification and speech recognition for 52 languages and dialects, streaming/offline inference and long audio transcription.
context: 0.6B / 1.7B ASR models, 52 languages and dialects, streaming + offline inference

name: Qwen3 TTS
description: State-of-the-art multilingual TTS with natural prosody and emotion control. Supports 30+ languages with streaming inference.

name: Sesame CSM
description: Conversational Speech Model — generates speech with natural turn-taking, backchannels and interruptions. Built specifically for multi-turn dialogue with real-time response generation.

name: Spark TTS
description: Bilingual TTS with virtual speaker creation — control pitch, speed, gender from text. Built on Qwen2.5 LLM backbone for powerful generation.

name: Step-Audio 2 Mini
description: Open-source multi-modal speech LLM. Unified understanding + generation in one model — ASR, TTS, voice conversion, speech dialogue. Strong expressive control and paralinguistic features. Available in Mini (8B) and Full variants.

name: StyleTTS 2
description: Style-based TTS with high naturalness and style diffusion. Academic research model with excellent quality.

name: Supertonic 3
description: Lightning-fast on-device TTS that runs with ONNX Runtime and no cloud call. Around 99M parameters, 31 languages, better reading stability and expression tags like laugh, breath and sigh.
voices: Preset voice styles + downloadable custom style embeddings
context: Open-weight ONNX model, 31 languages, practical local inference

name: TADA
description: LLM-based TTS built on Llama with a fully integrated audio tokenizer and decoder. Available in 1B (English) and 3B multilingual variants. Open-source weights on HuggingFace. Developed by Hume AI, specialists in expressive, emotion-aware voice.

name: Tortoise TTS
description: Quality-focused TTS with impressive voice cloning. Slower but produces very natural speech.

name: VibeVoice 1.5B
description: Open-source long-form multi-speaker TTS model (up to 90 min, up to 4 speakers). Listed as research-first with responsible-use constraints.
voices: Up to 4 speakers in long-form dialogue

name: VibeVoice ASR
description: Open-source multilingual ASR model (speech-to-text), supporting long-form transcription, timestamps, diarization and hotwords.

name: VibeVoice Realtime 0.5B
description: Open-source real-time streaming TTS model focused on low first-token latency (~300ms) and robust long-form generation.

name: Voicebox
description: Desktop app & orchestrator for local TTS — not a model. Provides a UI studio, voice profile management, and a local API. Generates audio via swappable backends (Qwen3 TTS, Kokoro, Piper, XTTS…). Think of it as a front-end shell that runs on top of your installed TTS models.
context: App layer — orchestrates TTS backends via local API

name: VoxCPM2
description: Tokenizer-free diffusion autoregressive TTS with 2B parameters, 30 languages, 48kHz output, voice design, controllable cloning and real-time streaming. Apache 2.0 and commercial-ready.
context: 2B params, 30 languages, 48kHz output, streaming RTF as low as ~0.3 on RTX 4090

name: WavTTS
description: Research-grade zero-shot TTS that generates speech directly in raw waveform space instead of mel spectrograms, codec tokens or VAE latents. High-fidelity EN/ZH voice cloning direction, but the official 16 kHz checkpoint is large and best for CUDA GPU setups.
voices: Zero-shot EN/ZH voice cloning from reference audio
context: Official 16 kHz checkpoint, direct raw waveform generation with flow matching + DiT

name: Whisper v3 Turbo
description: OpenAI's optimized Whisper v3 with 4 decoder layers instead of 32. 8× faster than Whisper Large v3 with only minor accuracy trade-off. 99 languages supported. New gold standard for fast local transcription.

name: XTTS v3 (Community)
description: Community-maintained successor to XTTS v2 after Coqui shut down. Improved cloning stability, lower artefacts, and 20+ languages. Drop-in replacement for existing XTTS pipelines with better prosody.

name: Zonos v0.1
description: 1.6B open-weight TTS with ultra-realistic zero-shot cloning from 5-30 s audio. Fine-grained controls: speaking rate, pitch, emotion (happy/sad/angry/fear). Streaming with ~200 ms first-token latency.
